passages.text: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus left that place.
He went to the region of Judea.
He went beyond the Jordan River.
Crowds came to Jesus again.
Jesus taught the crowds.
He often taught them.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς

passages.text: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees came to Jesus.
They wanted to test Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες Φαρισαῖοι ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι πειράζοντες αὐτόν

passages.text: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.
passages.sermon: Jesus replied to the Pharisees.\r\nHe asked them a question.\r\nHe said, “What did Moses command you?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς

passages.text: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to Jesus.
They answered His question.
They said Moses gave a command.
Moses allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce.
Moses allowed the man to send his wife away.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι

passages.text: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus addressed the people who questioned him about divorce.
He said, “Moses wrote this commandment for you.
Moses did this because your hearts were hard.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην

passages.text: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’
passages.sermon: God created the world in the beginning.\r\nGod made people at that time.\r\nGod made them male and female.
passages.original: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως Ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς

passages.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
passages.sermon:
God created people as male and female.
A man will leave his father.
A man will leave his mother.
He will join with his wife.
The man and his wife will become one flesh.
They are not two people anymore.
They are one flesh.
passages.original: Ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ

passages.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”
passages.sermon: God joins a man and a woman together in marriage.\r\nGod makes them one flesh.\r\nNo person should separate what God has joined.
passages.original: ὃ οὖν ὁ Θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω

passages.text: When they were back inside the house, the disciples asked Jesus about this matter.
passages.sermon: Jesus and His disciples entered the house.\r\nThe disciples spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey asked Jesus about this matter.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ περὶ τούτου ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν

passages.text: So He told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “Whoever divorces his wife commits a serious sin if he marries another woman.\r\nHe commits adultery against his first wife.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπ’ αὐτήν

passages.text: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples inside the house.
He explained the law about marriage.
If a woman divorces her husband,
and she marries another man,
she commits adultery.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον μοιχᾶται

passages.text: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
passages.sermon:
People brought little children to Jesus.
They wanted Jesus to place His hands on the children.
The disciples saw this.
The disciples rebuked the people who brought the children.
passages.original: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅψηται οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw what was happening.
Jesus felt indignant.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me.
Do not stop them.
The kingdom of God belongs to people like these children.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
A person must receive the kingdom of God like a little child.
If someone does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child, that person will never enter it.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν

passages.text: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.
passages.sermon: Jesus took the children in His arms.\r\nHe placed His hands on the children.\r\nJesus blessed the children.
passages.original: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτά

passages.text: As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up and knelt before Him. “Good Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus began to walk on the road.
A man saw Jesus.
The man ran to Jesus.
The man knelt before Jesus.
The man spoke to Jesus.
The man called Jesus “Good Teacher.”
The man asked Jesus a question.
He said, “What must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω

passages.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus asked, "Why do you call Me good?"
Only God is good.
No one else is good except God.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus listed God's commandments.
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not bear false witness.
Do not cheat others.
Honor your father.
Honor your mother.
passages.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας Μὴ φονεύσῃς Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς Μὴ κλέψῃς Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα

passages.text: “Teacher,” he replied, “all these I have kept from my youth.”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Jesus.
He called Jesus “Teacher.”
He said, “I have kept all these commandments.”
He said, “I have done this since I was young.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου

passages.text: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the man.
Jesus loved the man.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “You lack one thing.
Go.
Sell everything you own.
Give the money to the poor.
You will have treasure in heaven.
Then come.
Follow Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἕν σε ὑστερεῖ ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς τοῖς πτωχοῖς καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι

passages.text: But the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke with Jesus.
Jesus told the man to sell everything he owned and give to the poor.
The man heard these words.
The man became sad.
The man went away in sorrow.
The man had many possessions.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά

passages.text: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was the teacher and Son of God.
Jesus looked around at His disciples.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “It is hard for rich people to enter the kingdom of God.”
passages.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται

passages.text: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus said to them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
The disciples felt amazed at His words.
Jesus answered them again.
Jesus called them “Children.”
Jesus said it is hard to enter the kingdom of God.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς Τέκνα πῶς δύσκολόν ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν

passages.text: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus explained a truth about rich people and God's kingdom.
A camel is a large animal.
A needle has a very small hole called the eye.
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.
It is harder for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God than for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.
passages.original: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς ῥαφίδος διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν

passages.text: They were even more astonished and said to one another, “Who then can be saved?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples heard Jesus speak.
They became very astonished.
They spoke to each other.
They asked, “Who then can be saved?”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι

passages.text: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus looked at His disciples.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “This is impossible for people.
But it is not impossible for God.
God can do all things.
All things are possible with God.”
passages.original: Ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ πάντα γὰρ δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ

passages.text: Peter began to say to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed You.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Look, we have left everything.
We have followed You.”
passages.original: Ἤρξατο λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel will fail to receive a hundredfold in the present age—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
No one leaves home for Me and for the gospel without reward.
No one leaves brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields for Me and for the gospel without reward.
God will give that person a hundred times as much in this present time.
God will give houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields.
God will also allow persecutions in this present time.
In the age to come, God will give eternal life.
passages.original: Ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ μητέρα ἢ πατέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “Many people who are first now will be last later.\r\nMany people who are last now will be first later.”
passages.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι

passages.text: As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles, who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was leading His disciples on the road to Jerusalem.
The disciples followed Jesus.
The disciples felt amazed.
Other followers felt afraid.
Jesus took the Twelve disciples aside again.
Jesus began to tell them what would happen to Him.
Jesus said, “We are going up to Jerusalem.
The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes.
They will condemn Him to death.
They will deliver Him to the Gentiles.
The Gentiles will mock Him.
The Gentiles will spit on Him.
The Gentiles will flog Him.
The Gentiles will kill Him.
After three days, He will rise again.”
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο οἱ δὲ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται

passages.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
passages.sermon:
James and John were brothers.
Their father was Zebedee.
James and John came to Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν

passages.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to James and John.\r\nHe asked them a question.\r\nHe said, “What do you want me to do for you?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί θέλετε με ποιήσω ὑμῖν

passages.text: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”
passages.sermon:
James and John spoke to Jesus.
James and John were the sons of Zebedee.
They made a request to Jesus.
They said, “Let one of us sit at Your right hand.”
They also said, “Let the other sit at Your left hand.”
They asked for these places when Jesus comes in His glory.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς σου ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου

passages.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “You do not understand what you are asking.”
Jesus asked, “Are you able to drink the cup that I will drink?”
Jesus also asked, “Are you able to be baptized with the baptism that I will receive?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι

passages.text: “We can,” the brothers answered. “You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.
passages.sermon:
James and John spoke to Jesus.
James and John said, “We can.”
Jesus answered them.
Jesus said, “You will drink the cup that I drink.”
Jesus said, “You will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δυνάμεθα Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε

passages.text: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I cannot give the places at My right or My left.”
God has prepared these places for certain people.
Only those people will sit there.
passages.original: τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται

passages.text: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.
passages.sermon:
There were twelve disciples with Jesus.
James and John were two of these disciples.
The other ten disciples heard about what James and John had asked Jesus.
The ten disciples became angry with James and John.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου

passages.text: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus called His disciples together.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “You know something about rulers.
People see certain men as rulers over the Gentiles.
These rulers act as masters over the Gentiles.
Their great men use their power over the people.
They exercise authority over them.”
passages.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν

passages.text: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Among you, things will be different.
Anyone who wants to be great among you must serve you.
Anyone who wants to be first among you must become the slave of everyone.”
passages.original: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ μέγας γενέσθαι ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος

passages.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus did not come so that others would serve Him.
Jesus came to serve others.
Jesus came to give His life.
Jesus gave His life as a ransom for many people.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν

passages.text: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled with His disciples.
They came to the city of Jericho.
A large crowd followed Jesus and His disciples.
Jesus and the crowd began to leave Jericho.
A man named Bartimaeus sat beside the road.
Bartimaeus was blind.
Bartimaeus was a beggar.
Bartimaeus was the son of Timaeus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος τυφλὸς προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν

passages.text: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.sermon:
Bartimaeus was a blind beggar.
He sat beside the road near Jericho.
He heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
He began to cry out loudly.
He said, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.original: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ ἐλέησόν με

passages.text: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.sermon:
Many people told Bartimaeus to be quiet.
Bartimaeus was a blind beggar sitting beside the road.
Jesus was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a large crowd.
Bartimaeus did not stay silent.
He shouted even louder.
He said, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν Υἱὲ Δαυίδ ἐλέησόν με

passages.text: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was walking.
Jesus stopped.
Jesus spoke.
Jesus said, “Call him.”
The people obeyed Jesus.
The people called the blind man.
They spoke to the blind man.
They said, “Take courage!”
They said, “Get up!”
They said, “He is calling for you.”
passages.original: Καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Φωνήσατε αὐτόν Καὶ φωνοῦσιν τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ Θάρσει ἔγειρε φωνεῖ σε

passages.text: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Bartimaeus was blind.
Bartimaeus heard that Jesus was calling him.
Bartimaeus threw off his cloak.
Bartimaeus jumped up.
Bartimaeus came to Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the blind man.
Jesus asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
The blind man answered Jesus.
He said, “Rabboni, let me see again.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω Ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ραββουνι ἵνα ἀναβλέψω

passages.text: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Bartimaeus, who was blind.
Jesus said, “Go.”
Jesus said, “Your faith has healed you.”
Immediately, Bartimaeus could see.
Bartimaeus followed Jesus on the road.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ
